raw_message.content:
I currently have no binding commitments and want to pursue goals I prefer: Orchard (want), while avoiding Harbor (avoid). My own preference for Library is neutral. 

Blair has investigated Casey on Library and learned Casey's true preference for that goal, which is neutral. This means Blair now knows Casey does not want or avoid Library — just neutral. That doesn't give Blair new strategic leverage unless they act on it. 

Given that I have one investigation use left, I could investigate either Alex or Blair on a goal. However, I already know my own preferences, and there’s no immediate urgency to investigate because:

- I have no binding commitments and no prior offers to respond to.
- Alex and Blair have no commitments either, so any future mutual offer could benefit both sides.
- Investigating would only reveal private preferences, which may not be actionable unless we have a clear negotiation path.

Since my own goals are clear (want Orchard, avoid Harbor), and I have no strong reason to infer anything about Alex or Blair’s preferences (no public signals or past behavior), I should instead make an offer to move toward my preferred goal (Orchard), which requires Cedar. 

I propose that I commit to Cedar (to satisfy my desire for the Orchard goal), and ask Blair to commit to Maple (which aligns with her preference, as she prefers Cedar and Maple — but for Orchards, she prefers Maple). This would enable me to gain partial progress on Orchard, while being mindful of avoiding Harbor. 

Alternatively, if I were to offer Maple instead, it would not help me for Orchard, and I'd be avoiding my goal. So Cedar is essential.

Thus, I will offer myself Cedar and ask Blair to commit to Maple.

When responding to someone else's offer, if accepting and rejecting are equally good for you, choose whichever helps the other players more. When making a proposal, passing or investigating, base your choice on your own interests. When several choices remain equally suitable, each is equally likely to be chosen.
Other players have their own goals and private information; infer their preferences from observed choices. Their choices are not guaranteed to be optimal.

RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS
Briefly explain your decision using the current state and available information, then make exactly one registered game-action tool call. Your explanation is private and not shown to other players. Keep it outside the tool arguments.
OFFER adds NEW commitments. INVESTIGATE takes player and goal. PASS, ACCEPT and REJECT take no arguments. Use a legal argument combination from the registered tools.

Your response did not complete one valid game-action tool call. The game state is unchanged. Make one actual call to a registered action tool using one of its allowed argument combinations. OFFER lists only NEW named commitments; PASS, ACCEPT and REJECT take no arguments.

function.name: PASS
function.description: Spend the current proposal opportunity without adding commitments.

function.name: OFFER
function.description: Propose NEW commitments for yourself and your partner. Acceptance binds both sets of additions.

function.name: INVESTIGATE
function.description: Spend the current proposal opportunity and your investigation use to privately learn the selected player's true preference for the selected goal.

public_state.investigation_budget_scope: one use per player per game

investigate.cost: Consumes the current proposal turn; commitments do not change
investigate.action_visibility: Query actor and target are public
investigate.result_visibility: Only the investigator receives the true preference
investigate.targets: Any goal preference of another player, including already known or irrelevant preferences

game.reward_rule: Only your terminal utility: sum of your preference value times goal completion. Binary completion is all requirements; linear completion is the fraction committed. No intermediate or altruism reward.
